key_insight: Marked DeepHit predicts the joint probability of imminent delivery and fetal acidosis from labor-monitoring signals without assuming delivery timing is known.
clinical_relevance: This fetal-monitoring research—not cancer drug discovery—could support earlier recognition of acidemic delivery risk, but clinical benefit remains unproven.
method: Reframes continuous fetal heart rate and contraction monitoring as time-to-event prediction.
Adapts deep discrete-time survival models and marked point processes.
Models delivery timing and partially observed fetal acidosis labels jointly.
evidence_signal: Test-set AUROC for acidemic delivery within one hour was 0.837 (95% CI 0.692–0.970) at 6 hours into labor and 0.935 (0.858–0.964) at 12 hours; evaluations also included external validation at a second site.
watch_item: Prospective evaluation is needed to establish real-time reliability and clinical usefulness before deployment.
paper_title: Deep Time-to-Event Models for Intrapartum Fetal Monitoring
